d: Indonesia is Southeast Asia’s largest economy, boasting a $1.5 trillion GDP and the world’s richest reserves of nickel, the critical metal powering the global electric vehicle revolution. Yet behind high-speed trains and glittering skylines, an economic crisis is unfolding: nearly 10 million people have dropped out of the middle class, traditional manufacturing is collapsing, and foreign investors are pulling billions out of the market. How did a resource-rich economic tiger walk into an industrial trap?
